text: Mr. Ruppelt, an aeronautical engineer who formerly had the airport flying software investigation.
Mr. Ruppelt, when were you in the airport?
From 1951 until 1953.
And what were your duties there?
I was in charge of Project Blue Book. That was the Air Force's project investigate, identify flying object report.
And obviously you talked to many people who claimed to have seen flying objects.
Several thousand.
Did you believe that these people were victims of hallucinations?
No, not all of them.
What percentage would you say you thought had some credibility?
I'd say about 20% of them.
Have you ever actually seen any evidence that proved that there were flying objects unidentified?
No, I'm certain.
Absolutely not.
Now, were you working for the government to be at what percentage of credibility on any of these reports?
Enough validity that we spent a good deal of time and money to investigate them.
Were the investigations thorough?
Yes, they were.
And you tell us if the Air Force is still thorough in investigating this problem.
I'm not the alma mater, but I'm afraid that after years and years,
if I find any answers, they're sort of slacked off a little bit.
Of course, there's renewed interest in it now.
You brought some of it out today, and I believe a colonel tested very clearly.
Yes, of course.
If there are flying objects, do you think they're coming from outer space or another planet?
Well, if my answer to the question is only an opinion, I backed up any scientific facts, so I think I'll stand behind a fifth amendment on that one.
Well, I'll try to once again prevent any killing from another foreign power, Your Honor.
I doubt this very much.
You don't present any credibility in the statements we've heard tonight, the statements we've read in the paper about foreign accidents?
No.
I'm not going to explain you these stories.
Yes, I realize that, but I don't believe you.
No, I don't.
Now, as an aeronautical engineer, how do you feel the identity and
confirmation of these flying objects could be learned or should be learned?
Well, I think that the next step, if the Air Force feels that there is a next step necessary,
is to go into a rather elaborate instrumentation program, something very similar to the Moonwatch program
that they've got to track this buttoning.
It would be expensive, but it would come up with the answer or no answer,
and either one of them would be very significant.
So what's going on? What's happening?
Very definitely. I feel just standing behind Peter Z is nothing but a very detrimental to the whole project.
Thanks very much, Mr. Ruppelt. It's an awful fall.
Now, maybe there's really nothing to this flying saucer scare.
At least that's what I keep telling myself, but I'm afraid that I tend to believe myself just a little bit less every time I say it.
The obvious conclusion, as Mr. Ruppelt just said,
The conclusion, I think, that we've reached in this whole report is that the time is now
right for the government to tell us what it knows, if it knows anything.
